listings.title: 1967 International Scout 800 SUV
listings.description:
Vintage Chicago Mail Truck in GREAT condition. I purchased it from a farmer in Southern Illinois in 2011. He used it as his ranch truck. He bought it at a city auction (didn't remember the year) and kept it in a barn. Never drove it off the property. Now it sits in my garage and is a weekend joy rider.
The good:
- Original Comanche Scout motor. It is literally 1/2 of a v8 engine. They called it the "slant 4". 152 ci 3 speed with high/low 4x4
- Rebuild carb with a 2 barrel Motorcraft 5200 (Weber 32/36 clone)
- Pentronix ignition (original choke knob still on the dash, but not connected)
- Replaced hoses
- Re-cored the radiator
- new front and rear U joints
- newer shocks (previous owner)
- new water pump
- new clutch master and slave cylinders
- Switched out old vacuum wipers with modern (vintage looking) electric
- New wiper squirter
- New leaf springs
- Previous owner did a light restoration and replaced a few rusty floor boards with heavy gauge sheet metal. Body is original and virtually rust and dent free! But if you want to find some rust, you’ll find it underneath if you poke around
- Interior sprayed with bed liner
- New body bushings
- New fuel pump
- New exhaust system
- Rebuilt the front steering knuckles.
- Rewired and functional turn signals, brake lights, interior “courtesy” light and back up lights.
- It has the D27 axles front and rear, four wheel drive high and low operate. The heater works and the glass is all intact. 
- I also have a white wall spare tire and vintage rear tire mount that has not been installed (I like seeing the tail gate logo)
- The odometer reads 30xxx miles. ALL mechanics I have talked to believe the odometer has never rolled over.
- 2WD/4WD HI/Low all functional. Has original lock out hubs up front.
- Starts every time. Runs and drives great. Get's lots of smiles.
Here’s the bad:
- Needs upholstery! I have cheap seat covers on it now. The seats are all original Scout seats that are structurally sound, but new upholstery is needed.
- Time for some new brake shoes
 Gas gauge doesn’t work. Don’t you even get me started on this one. This is common on Scout 800’s. I've repaired it multiple times, but it just stops working a few days later. My new trick... fill the tank every 50 miles and you'll be fine.
International Scout made around 7000 right hand drives for the US Postal Service between 1966 and 1987 (when Jeep got the new contract). According to my research, it is estimated that there are very few survivors today (less than 200), so this is a bit of a rare bird and rather collectable for Scout enthusiasts. 
You have to know what you are getting into with an old Scout. No power steering. No power brakes. Top speed is 45mph. A super fun truck on summer days with the top off!
Cash only. No exceptions.

Plugs replaced recently (per maintenance schedule)
Oil was changed approx 200 miles ago. Same with transmission fluid. It has been done every 80,000 miles. 
Currently on odo is just over 180,000. These Toyota cars easily get 250,000. There is a lot of life left in it. 
It has had 2 accidents. First was an inattentive driver entering the road and hit the car in the driver side rear wheel. Repair was new wheel and rear fender cover. 
The 2nd was this last winter when a deer was hit at 30mph. The repair was new front bumper cover, passenger fender, wheel-well liner some other plastic parts and I replaced both headlights at the same time since it was apart and easy. 
These box’s are simple to work on which makes them popular in the mod circles. 
Currently averaging 29-30 mpg. 
It pulls hard to 100mph. 
This is a great car, tons of interior space, is safe and maintained. 
Only way to appreciate it is to try it. 
Price is negotiable but I do have a low limit and I’m not desperate to unload the car. 
Until it sells, this is still a daily driver. Weekdays it will be in Green Lake; evenings and weekends it is in Omro. 
Call and text is best. If you call, leave a message and I’ll call back as fast as I can. 
Single owner and never left Wisconsin.

listings.description:
Own a piece of automotive history with this authentic 1966 Ford Mustang GT 2+2 Fastback. A true survivor vehicle, it features its original A-Code 289 CID 4BBL V8 engine paired with a classic 4-speed manual transmission. Carefully maintained within a private collection for over two decades, this vintage muscle car combines incredible originality with reliable performance.
The exterior is dressed in a factory-correct Turquoise Metallic paint finish applied over 20 years ago, highlighting excellent chrome accents, trim, and all-original glass. Inside, the cabin features the iconic original turquoise-and-white Pony Interior, complete with comfortable bucket seats, a full center console, a convenient fold-down rear seat, rally pack gauges, and a factory tachometer. All interior lights and the clock remain fully operational.
Further adding to its charm, this classic fastback includes a Cobra engine dress-up kit, an unmodified trunk and undercarriage, classic rally wheels, and a preserved 1979 Georgia State inspection sticker pointing to its rich Southern heritage. Freshly serviced with a new fuel tank, fresh fluids, a professional tune-up, new tires, and a replacement battery, this vintage Mustang GT Fastback is completely ready to drive, show, and enjoy.

listings.title: 1991 Oldsmobile Custom Cruiser
listings.description:
Selling my '91 Olds Custom Cruiser. Color is Black Sapphire. These are very hard to find, but mechanically they are identical to a Chevy Caprice or Buick Roadmaster, so replacement parts are easy to find. The body definitely has it's share of cosmetic defects, dings and the paint has some scratches, but it polishes up nicely. 
Only around 11,000 Custom Cruisers were built between 1991 and 1992, so these are extremely hard to find in this condition with a solid frame and floor pans. Car spent most of its life around South Carolina, and has only seen a few Iowa winters. These have the folding rear-facing 3rd row seat, so they can seat up to 8 people.
Fuel injected 305 V8, 700R4 trans, (Jasper rebuild) RWD, no fluid leaks, frame is in great shape, and the car only has a few rust spots, the lower B-pillars, and the spare tire well. Zero rust in the D-pillars. Odometer shows 160,xxx miles, actual mileage is approximately 135k. (Original gauge cluster failed, and was replaced with a higher mileage unit). Tires all have good tread.
Recent service: oil change, rear limited slip differential service, power steering pump, water pump, serpentine belt, air filter, rear shocks. I'm sure I am forgetting things.
The interior is in pretty nice shape, but could use a few finishing pieces: The dashboard has been cut a bit underneath the carpeted dash cover. Driver's window works well, but the other three are slow and a bit finicky. The stereo does not work. 
It has the upgraded center console from a Buick Roadmaster, but the original is included.
Also the wiper arms were upgraded to newer Buick Lesabre arms, which do a much better job than the originals.
The fuse is unplugged for the electronic climate control, as the blower motor resistor needs to be replaced. It will drain the car battery over time. A battery disconnect switch has been added, and it works great.
The car comes with a clean title, plenty of extra parts, two extra Oldsmobile rims, and I do have a set of Buick Roadmaster wheels on good Firestone snow tires that can be added.
The engine has an exhaust manifold leak, and smokes a bit if it sits for long periods of time due to burning some oil.
It would be an awesome candidate for an LS swap, or even a hot small block would bolt right in if you wanted more performance.
Overall it drives very well and rides great. Running and driving easy project. 
$3650 for a very cool collectable wagon, Come check it out!

I'm out of time and patience and not paying another shop to not fix it so we bought something newer before the snow flies. 
It's a rusty MN truck but it handles and brakes like new. Decent A/T tires, Stainless brake lines, poly fuel lines.

I'm beginning to think it may be a faulty alternator (that I replaced last year) and/or a bad ground, I ran it the other day and it ran great now that it started getting cold till it died and the 2 year old battery was dead after running for 20+ min.
Fuel gauge doesn't work so set your trip for mileage. Also comes with the new cv axle, wheel hub bearing and sway bar links for the other side I didn't get around to putting on before it started running like crap. Needs a windshield but not much else if you can make it run. 
If I can't get $2k for it, I'm either donating to it a veterans organization or parting it out next spring, so please don't waste our time.
Call/text/email with any questions. $2000 cash only

listings.title: 2003 MINI Cooper S
listings.description:
2003 Mini Cooper S
Very clean, 38 mpg, COLD A/C, HOT heat, Supercharged with 6 speed manual. Very fun car to drive!
Background on the car- Bought the car from a 45 year old Mini Cooper enthusiast. He was very meticulous and knew absolutely everything about a Mini Cooper a guy could know, and he had a few different Mini's. He did the normal tasteful modifications to the car for a Mini Cooper of its Era as well as maintenance too. Supercharger oil, pulley, Alta tune, Alta air filter, cat back exhuast, Cooling fan relay mod, larger intercooler. I have had zero issues with the car in the last several years ive owned it. My Wife and I just drove it out to Green Bay, WI recently (4.5hr one way; 9hr round trip). Thats how dependable and trustworthy it is... and we have 3 other daily drivers to use. I just drive it and listen to the cool supercharger noises. I dont beat on it, I never race it, I just drive it to commute around (it fits everywhere) and its fun to drive around. 
-Car is equipped with the fuel efficient 1.6L Supercharged 4 cylinder engine. Powerful and peppy powertrain for the car. The car is rated at 38MPG on the highway and around 29MPG in city type driving and it gets at least that if not better. Very smooth and comfortable car with regular maintenance completed. I bought the car about 3 years ago because I've always wanted a Mini, fun to drive, it fits in any parking spot, and the great fuel mileage. Car has mostly been commuted on the freeway and has very well maintained easy highway miles... has roughly 161k miles on it. Has newer brakes, oil change, etc recently done.
-Mechanically the car is great in my opinion considering the age. The engine runs as smooth as a swiss watch and has all of the power that it did like it was new (actually significantly more). Has no issues that would need attention (just drove it 9hrs round trip)!! The transmission shifts perfectly and nice and smooth, clutch is in good shape and it is very easy to drive. The steering is nice and tight and drives straight down the road. The brakes are powerful and responsive (newer). The suspension rides great and is tight and comfortable. Tires are still good, about 70% tread remaining. HOT Heat and COLD A/C!!!!!!
It is a 2003 Mini so with that its not perfect but miniscule such as the parking brake needs to be adjusted, the drivers window needs to be adjusted (I put a window regulator in and I didnt get it adjusted perfect but its very close), could use a valve cover gasket if you wanted but not needed right away. Id drive it to any state in the country today from AZ to FL to NY and not think twice. 
-Car is equipped nicely.... Heated seats (very hot and work great), power windows, power locks, power mirrors, Great Stereo, Navigation that does work, Map lights, rear seats fold down, CRUISE CONTROL, 6 way adjust seat, Lots of storage compartments, remote trunk release, Keyless entry, and much more that im sure im forgetting.
-The interior is in great shape and clean, no major staining. It has the rare and sought after blue leather interior. Nearly no visible signs of any type of wear on the seats, carpet, buttons etc. It really is that nice. the car has been kept perfectly clean and treated with respect. Everything on the interior works... windows, buttons, lights etc, everything.
-The exterior is clean for the year of the vehicle. Paint has a great glossy shine to it. Has no major body damage or major dents. Car was always kept clean on the outside just like it was on the inside and it shows. It does have the typical parking lot door ding and scratch/scuff... you have to look for them but they are there here or there. Minor rust bubble on the rear but nothing major or noticeable. 
Very reliable car that needs nothing but a driver. All maintenance done and is ready to go. We would drive this car across country over and over and not think twice.
Clean and clear title in hand signed and ready to go.

Upgrading to something larger for our fam

Located in Grand Rapids, 28th and Kalamazoo-ish area. Come see it, let me know if you have any questions.
NO trades please
__________
12 year old used car notes & disclaimers :) 
It tends to burn oil (like many older vehicles do). Just be sure to stay on top of oil changes and checking it. 
The check engine light likes to come on and off. It throws an emissions/EVAP code. We have had it into our shop a few different times – they replaced the EVAP Purge Valve and the Cannister Purge Valve and ran a smoke test and there are no leaks. It seems to be a wiring issue and I didn't have interest in paying to fix it. I have an ODB2 scanner (included) so I can see what the codes are to ensure it is not a different issue but since the evap codes don't affect the drivability it is more an annoyance than anything else, but worth noting. The dash also sometimes will pop a "check fuel cap" notice which we have also replaced.
If I was keeping it I'd probably put on a new set of tires for winter, but they have some life in them still

listings.title: 2008 MINI Cooper Hatchback
listings.description:
For sale is a 2008 Mini Cooper. I am the second owner. I've owned it since 167,000 miles.
Look at known issues below. It is not a perfect car, but it's enjoyable to drive. I've enjoyed it two summers. But I am the only one in my family that can drive stick and we need a car that is automatic that we all can share.
I frequently drive this car between Eau Claire, Menomonie, and the Twin Cities. I drive this car pretty conservatively, so I am getting consistently 45 mpg with it. It takes premium gas.
Recently replaced:
• spark plugs
• rear brakes, rotors, and calipers
• oil change about 1,500 miles ago
Known issues:
• oil leak - needs a quart of oil every 1,000-1,500 miles
• exhaust leak - it makes a little noise, and when the heat is on and you're sitting at a stoplight you can smell a little bit of it (I just turn the heat off if the car is idling for a while)
• passenger power window is finicky - it works fine, but it can't go all the way up sometimes--you have to work it up gently
• air conditioning does not work - it has not work for about two years - I never looked into it
• tires - the back two tires leak air, one more than the other - I usually have to air them up once a week
• driver's seat has wear and is torn
• center console information display (time, audio input) sometimes is faded and can't see it

listings.description:
One-owner 2016 Hyundai Sonata Hybrid Limited with the Ultimate Package, bought new and selling because it now sits unused in our garage. Clean Wisconsin title in hand, no accidents, no liens, never smoked in. Located in New Berlin / Milwaukee, WI. Contact via Craigslist email only.
Asking $9,825 — the top of KBB private-party value for very good condition (see last photo), priced there for the new engine and the recent work below.
Features (Limited with Ultimate Package)
- Panoramic sunroof, leather seats, heated and ventilated front seats, heated rear seats
- Infinity premium audio, Apple CarPlay / Android Auto, navigation
- Blind-spot detection, rear cross-traffic alert, lane departure warning, forward collision warning, smart cruise control, rear parking sensors, backup camera
- Push-button start with proximity key, driver's seat memory
- Averaging ~37 MPG on the trip computer
Condition
- Never smoked in, no substance use in the car. No accidents, no submersion or water damage.
- Two small cosmetic flaws near the rear passenger-side door and bumper — a dent on the chrome trim and a white scratch — both shown in the photos.
- Pre-purchase inspection welcome at your expense.
Engine — the important part
- New engine long block installed under warranty by Rosen Hyundai of Greenfield in August 2024, after the original engine seized at about 66,000 miles. Invoice and paperwork available to show.
- About 27,500 miles on the replacement engine.
- The replacement is covered for connecting-rod bearing failure to 15 years / 150,000 miles from original delivery, and the coverage transfers to the next owner (Hyundai TXXM extension, KSDS installed — paperwork available).
- Hybrid battery is original; its 10-year / 100,000-mile transferable coverage is nearly used up at this mileage.
Recent work
- Michelin CrossClimate2 tires, all-season with severe-snow (3PMSF) rating — 7/32" front, 8/32" rear
- Hybrid starter-generator (HSG) belt replaced — original belt, never changed before
- Engine air filter and cabin filter replaced, oil changed
- New 12V battery, summer 2026
Included: 2 key fobs, original Hyundai cargo net, original purchase documents, engine-replacement invoice and TXXM warranty letter. VIN available on request so you can run a history check.
Payment: wire transfer, or a cashier's check issued together at your bank. No personal checks, no Zelle/Venmo. We meet at a bank in daylight; funds confirmed before I sign the title.
Please, no lowball offers — the price is set at the top of KBB for the reasons above.

RARE 2002 LINCOLN BLACKWOOD
Produced for only one production year and with fewer than 3,500 total units sold, this luxury truck is extremely rare, which is a major factor in its collectability
FOR RESTORATION OR FOR PARTS
RUNS WELL, EVERYTHING WORKS

HISTORY FROM HEMMINGS MARKETPLACE STORIES - The Blackwood was powered by a 300-horsepower, 5.4-liter DOHC V8 engine, a more potent and exclusive powertrain than what was offered in the Ford F-150 on which it was based.powered by a 300-horsepower, most distinctive and controversial feature of the Blackwood was its rear cargo area, which was unlike any pickup before it. Instead of a traditional open bed, Lincoln opted for a permanently mounted, power-operated tonneau cover that sealed a fully carpeted and LED-lit cargo compartment. The sides of this “trunk” were finished with polished aluminum and an attractive black woodgrain laminate with aluminum strakes, evoking the classic “woodie” wagons. The rear featured split “barn doors” instead of a traditional tailgate, further emphasizing its departure from conventional truck utility. While this design offered a secure, weather-sealed space larger than a Town Car’s trunk, it severely limited the vehicle’s practicality, alienating traditional truck buyers who valued open-bed functionality.
The interior of the Blackwood was a direct carry-over from the Navigator, a sign that Lincoln prioritized luxury above all else. It featured a plush four-seat configuration with Connolly leather and real burl walnut wood trim, a level of sophistication previously unseen in the pickup segment. The front seats were both heated and cooled, a forward-thinking comfort feature for the era. 
The Lincoln Blackwood holds a unique position in automotive history as a bold experiment in luxury truck design, making it a highly desirable and interesting vehicle for collectors and enthusiasts alike. With fewer than 3,500 total units sold, this luxury truck is extremely rare, which is a major factor in its collectability.
The Lincoln Blackwood is a coveted truck today due to its rarity, unique design, and status as a luxury pioneer in a market that was once exclusively utilitarian. Despite its commercial failure, its one-of-a-kind features make it a unique conversation starter and a sought-after item for collectors.

listings.description: All original 1983 Cadillac Seville. It was driven by Meta Michell, wife of Bill Mitchell who was the chief of design at General Motors. I purchased four years ago from the guy in Detroit who had purchased it, and had it shipped to me in Clinton Iowa. You can find the You Tube video of the Mitchell Museum if you just google it. The front windows work, but the two backseat ones do not. I think all lights and signals work. I need to sell to recoup my garage space and I need the cash to travel on bucket list trips. The only work I’ve had performed was replacing the bumper fillers which were all broken when I purchased the car.

listings.title: 2012 Ford Mustang Convertible
listings.description:
VIN: 
Clean title.
Last purchase was 3-26-2021 at 113535 miles. Grandma driven in the country and stored during winter, driven occasionally in nice weather until this year. Odometer is at around 125300 miles as of 11-11-2026.
This Mustang was optioned with the leather steering wheel and rear spoiler. Has 4 carpet floor mats and Weathertech liners for the driver and front passenger.
 
These 2010-2014 models have cosmetic issues with hood lip paint bubbling, door card leather peeling, and steering wheel buttons flaking. 
We did a sand and repaint on the hood lip about 3 years ago; it could use a touch up (see photos).
For the peeling door leather, I tried aftermarket panels but those are cheap hard feeling glossy plastics molded to appear leather, so I cut my own soft touch vinyl instead as replacements. 
Buttons have minimal wear. 
There are a few tiny knicks and dings (see above photos).
May need standard maintenance just due to age, but it runs and drives fantastic.

listings.title: 2003 Ford Focus SVT
listings.description:
I collect SVT's. Actually I've owned 2% of them over the last 17 years so I know a little bit about these cars. Not 100% rust free but it is southern clean, EAP means European Appearance Package Approximately 2000 of the 14,000 SVTs had came as EAP's. The option included Recaro Seats, the pictured 17 Spoke wheels and HID headlights. This car currently has aftermarket headlights.
 I bought it in Orlando with a snapped timing belt. I started swapping the head on it in Florida but ultimately flat towed it back to Wisconsin and finished up the job. New timing belt with proper tensioner. New water pump. I added the proper header heat shield so many people tear off when it starts rattling (secured it as well) The car has an Off Road Pipe (No cat) and no CEL so it is presumably tuned. Scoots along better than average. Someone added a 'Dual Exhaust' out the back, fairly well done.The clutch pedal feels a bit stiffer than normal so I'm guessing it has someone's stage II clutch in it. Ebrake still works, southern cars are so nice to work on but the heat beats them up cosmetically. Not sure who painted the passenger door and with what but it is rust free. If you want to restore this Gem I'd have a nice silver door, the proper HID headlights I'd include and a few other parts for the restoration. Something is mad in the sunroof, you have to help it closed but it does function, parts would be included, ABS light says it needs a 'pump' I can include that. 
It has Steeda Springs in it (I'm not immediately familiar) so it has a slightly lower stance. Drilled rotors, the 6 speed shifts great. Drives like a big go-cart - which is what makes them so popular for autocross, road courses and just a fun daily! This would be a good candidate for a wrap, pick a cool color like a gloss gray (like clear coated primer, that is currently trendy) 
If you want to strip it and make a race car I've got others. Absolutely as is 3000, with the parts to make it nice 3500. I do have a WI dealers license, On Track Auto, so WI residents will be charged Tax, title and plate fees as necessary. Out of staters get the title can are responsible for that themselves at home. THANKS, Matt
I'll get some more pics, interior needs some love but not lived in by dogs, the underneath pics will show it's worthy.
